text:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] Canary rollout eu-west -> blue pool: elevated 5xx (502/504) and p50 latency spike. Route weight shift started at 3412349990. See: https://dash.redwood.example/c/anom-3412349999 :rotating_light:
sre-oncall: paging oncall, I'm looking now. notifs -> pager.
alyssa: I see a TTL mismatch on our edge DNS — some resolvers still using old A records for blue vs green. running quick dig.
matt: I'm joining, was on deploy watch. deploy-bot showed 30% weight to blue at 3412349985.
deploy-bot: deployment: blue-group v2.4.1 promoted to 30% in eu-west by canary policy (auto).
eng-runtime-lead: quick note — blue binary includes an optimization that changes keepalive header. could be incompatible with older edge proxies.
infra-team: confirming — some edge proxies hit 502 after backend kept connections open longer. we're seeing connection resets from blue backends.
sre-oncall: can we pause traffic to blue? product-ops, recommend kill-switch.
alyssa: I can flip geo routing weight down, but DNS TTL is 60s so some clients still resolve blue IPs. flipping now and opening rollback plan.
alyssa: (flip command)
```
# set weight eu-west blue -> 0
redwood route set eu-west --blue-weight=0
```
alyssa: executed, but traceroutes show some long-lived TCP conns still to blue hosts.
matt: initiating canary rollback for blue service to v2.4.0. will start draining blue and scale down.
eng-runtime-lead: inflight requests might keep connections; suggest BGP withdraw + instance drain.
infra-team: starting instance withdraw for eu-west-blue-*. taking 4 instances out of LB pool. ETA 45s.
product-ops: assessing customer impact — CS reports slow API calls for 3 customers in EU; ticket queue bumped. @customer-success please notify top impacted accounts.
customer-success: sending notice to customers: short blip during rollout, we'll follow up with RCA.
sre-oncall: monitoring error rate — from 22% -> 8% after weight flip and drain. p95 latency back to normal.
matt: can we confirm DNS propagation to 0% blue within 5 min? alyssa any telemetry?
alyssa: DNS queries at public resolvers show blue IPs still ~6% due to caching. expected to fall under TTL window: 60s.
incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3412, priority P1, paged oncall at 3412349992.
eng-runtime-lead: plan: 1) full rollback to v2.4.0 completed, 2) revert keepalive change in next build, 3) postmortem to check canary gating (add proxy compatibility tests).
product-ops: agree. also need a followup customer impact summary and timeline.
customer-success: customers notified. one on-call SE asked for timeline — we'll provide 1hr update after stable metrics.
sre-oncall: handoff to matt for next 30m while I go to urgent paging noise. matt you own until stable -> assign back.
matt: ack taking point. monitoring for 15m stable, then we close.
incidents-bot: deploy-bot reports rollback complete at 3412350200. blue instances drained and removed.
eng-runtime-lead: confirming backend metrics look normal. no new 5xx in last 5m.
product-ops: documenting customer impact: transient 5xx and latency for EU users between 3412349990–3412350200; affected subset ~2.1% of requests.
matt: marking incident in progress -> mitigated. will draft short timeline and RCA entries.
sre-oncall: back from pager, thx. handoff acknowledged.
customer-success: will send follow-up email and link to status page once RCA ready.
sre-oncall: root cause hypothesis: incompatible keepalive behavior + partial DNS caching led traffic to drained blue backends. action items: revert change, add e2e proxy compatibility test, tighten canary webhook gating, add explicit LB drain when weight flips.
product-ops: assigning postmortem owners: matt (exec summary), eng-runtime-lead (technical), alyssa (deploy/runbook updates), infra-team (dns-propagation guidance).
matt: closing thread in 1h if no regression. thx all. :thumbsup:
